name: Neo-Legionarism
summary: Neo-Legionarism is the post-1989 Romanian movement of groups that claim the tradition of Corneliu Zelea Codreanu's Legion of the Archangel Michael (the Iron Guard). Its ideology fuses fascism, ethnic nationalism, anti-Semitism, Romanian folklore, mysticism and Orthodox Christianity, and it venerates Codreanu and the Legion's martyrs. Through Codreanu's own texts it rejects democracy and parties for rule by a selected elite under a monarch, subordinates the individual to an eternal nation of the living and the dead, and seeks a spiritual rebirth and a 'new man'.
scope: The defining scholarship presents neo-Legionarism as groups that, after 1989, 'defined themselves as Legionary, thereby entering into the tradition of the Iron Guard' founded by Codreanu, expressing their message 'mainly ... through references to Codreanu's movement' (Endresen, s6), and that 'promoted principles promoted by Legionary Movement's leader, Corneliu Codreanu' (Simion, s7). The profile therefore answers from those scholarly accounts and from Codreanu's own canonical texts, For My Legionaries (s2) and The Nest Leader's Manual (s10). It does not answer from the programmes of individual organisations (Noua Dreapta, Everything for the Country, the Movement for Romania) or from parties such as AUR, and the interwar Legion's brief rule in 1940-41 is not neo-Legionarism's record.

The scholarship that lists neo-Legionaries' modern positions (Endresen 2010, whose abstract alone is open; it is the source Wikipedia cites for opposition to the EU, NATO, the UN, immigration, homosexuality, abortion and drugs) is paywalled (CEEOL, academia.edu login), so those statements are null; Andreescu's Extremismul de dreapta in Romania (2003) was read but does not name neo-Legionarism and is not cited. Themes searched: economy (creed, land, unions, finance), government (democracy, elite, monarchy, parties, elections), society and culture (nation, race, religion, family, education), world (territory, minorities clause, communism, invasion), liberty (rights, death penalty, censorship), means (violence, revolution, work camps). Ecology, technology, globalism and most modern social issues have no source.
